column1: # The optional 5th column narrows an entry to ONE sub-unit of the file — for
# the module sweep, one of spthy/spthytyped/msr. Left empty (or absent) the
# entry covers every row of the file, so a file ledgered for `msr` only still
# reports a fresh `spthy` divergence as DIFF.
# The optional 6th column narrows to ONE SYMPTOM, matched against the first
# word of the row's detail field (`stdout`, `stderr`, `json`, `dot`, `rc`,
# `both-fail-stdout`, `timeout/kill`). Without it an entry excuses whatever
# goes wrong with that file — a stderr-named class with no symptom column will
# LEDGER a fresh stdout regression on the same file, so give every entry the
# apply_ledger reports entries that have stopped excusing anything on stderr:
# LEDGER-STALE (all its rows came back OK), LEDGER-UNMATCHED (it matched no row
# at all — the file left the corpus, or a file-wide entry shadows it) and
# LEDGER-DUP (two entries share a path+sub-unit key, so only the last is live).
#   stderr-oracle-calls    HS derivation checks invoke the theory's oracle
#                          heuristic and emit ">>>> START ... Oracle call"
#                          stderr blocks; RS deriv checks never call oracles.
#   capacity               RS aborts (rc 134, stack/OOM at the 16GiB guard) or
#                          both sides exhaust the 600s retry cap. A
#                          timeout/kill class — see below: reports UNCOMPARED,
#   TIMEOUT/KILL ENTRIES CERTIFY NOTHING. Two classes here — `capacity` and
#   `oracle-timeout` — carry the symptom `timeout/kill`, which means a side was
#   killed at the cap and the row compared NOTHING. apply_ledger terminates such
#   a row as UNCOMPARED rather than LEDGERED, and sweep_finish prints it as its
#   own UNCOMPARED=n figure beside the verdict on the DONE line: visible on
#   every run, never folded into the clean count, and deliberately not fatal
#   (the cap is a property of the box). An UNDOCUMENTED timeout/kill row stays
#   ERROR and FAILS the sweep, so writing one down here is what makes it quiet —
#   and all it buys is "we know this row is uncovered", not "this row passed".
#   Which is why such an entry must name the CAP and nothing else. "HS blew the
#   cap, RS finished" is a claim about the BOX, not the port, and it goes stale
#   the moment the machine gets faster or the oracle's cache warms: the two U2F
#   entries carried a timeout class while their actual divergence was
#   stderr-simplifier-trace, and it masked every other symptom on those files
#   meanwhile. If you OBSERVED a divergence, classify by the divergence and give
#   the entry that symptom (`hs-derivcheck-timeout` is the cap CAUSING an
#   observed stdout divergence, so its symptom is `stdout` and it reports
#   LEDGERED); reach for capacity/oracle-timeout only when the run produced no
#   (No replay-empty-json class exists. A json export that replays to `sorry`
#    is a LOCAL replay-matcher fault, not the #874 numbering/eq-store class:
#    check that the stored goal text round-trips through the AC signature
#   sapic-export-echo      sapic/export corner files whose -m echo/rc diverged
#                          The pinned HS oracle predates that fix.
#   stored-proof-echo      stored-proof replay divergence: RS adds an unmatched
#                          `by sorry` branch and `/* unannotated */` markers to

#    "[Saturating Sources]" lines on both sides, so that divergence — both
